subject: AstraPay integration: SDK setup, endpoint migration & retry strategy
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rios <elena.rios@astrapay.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AstraPay integration: SDK setup, endpoint migration & retry strategy

Hey Elena — thanks again for the sync today. Attaching a short checklist and code bundle (sdk-snippets.tar.gz) to get your engineers started. Proposed agenda for the first-week runway: 

- Day 0: access & credentials (API keys scoped to sandbox), network allowlist
- Day 1: SDK install + hello-world (Node + Go examples attached)
- Day 2: endpoint migration plan (v1 -> v2) and smoke tests
- Day 3: retries/timeouts and rate-limit handling (integration tests)
- Day 4: cutover rehearsal + production rollout window

A few operational constraints up front: we recommend client-side timeouts of 10s for generation endpoints, a request-level idempotency token for any non-idempotent calls, and exponential backoff with full jitter for retries. I've pasted key snippets in the attachment and below for quick reference.

Quick ask: can your platform team confirm a sandbox IP to allowlist and an estimate for traffic pattern (steady TPS vs spikes)? If you can share, we will pre-configure batching and cache settings to optimize latency/cost.

Attachments: AstraPay_onboarding_checklist.pdf, sdk-snippets.tar.gz

— Vivek
Head of CSM Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rios <elena.rios@astrapay.com>

Subject: Re: AstraPay integration: SDK setup, endpoint migration & retry strategy

Thanks Vivek — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs before we schedule the sandbox window:

1) Our backend is mostly Go; do you recommend the native Go SDK or the REST route as a stopgap? We prefer minimal infra changes early on.
2) For endpoint migration: we have an internal v1 API integrated today. Can you call out a lightweight rollback approach if we see regressions?

On the TPS: our payments flows are bursty on settlement days (up to ~120 reqs/s for a 5–10 minute window) and quiet otherwise (~2–5 reqs/s).

I'll loop in a couple of infra engineers once you confirm the allowlist needs.

— Elena
Senior Platform PM, AstraPay

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rios <elena.rios@astrapay.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Sep 2028 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AstraPay integration: SDK setup, endpoint migration & retry strategy

Hi Elena — short answers then a pragmatic plan below.

1) Go SDK vs REST: start with the Go SDK (we maintain it + it supports request batching and automatic token refresh). If you need a stopgap, REST + simple client wrapper works fine for the very first day.

2) Rollback approach for endpoint migration: we recommend a layered rollout with traffic shadowing, canary at 5/25/100% and immediate automatic fallback to v1 on error spike or increased latency. See the three-step plan below.

Practical runbook (I'll own D2-D4 with our implementation engineer):

- Preflight (before any code change):
  - We create sandbox API keys (scope=read,write: sandbox) and a short-lived test account.
  - Allowlist Redwood sandbox IPs: 34.120.45.12, 2607:f8b0:4006:80f::200e (placeholder — we'll provide final CIDRs)
  - Share a lightweight test harness (we'll drop in your repo) that runs ~500 synthetic calls/min for 10 minutes to validate batching and KV cache behavior.

- D1 (SDK setup + hello-world):
  - Node (example):
    - npm i @redwoodai/sdk
    - example.js:
      const Redwood = require('@redwoodai/sdk');
      const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, baseURL: 'https://api.redwood.ai/v2' });
      (async () => {
        const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-embed-1', prompt: 'hello' });
        console.log(r.output);
      })();

  - Go (example):
    // go.mod -> module github.com/astrapay/redwood-sample
    package main
    import (
      "context"
      "fmt"
      "github.com/redwoodai/go-sdk"
    )
    func main() {
      c := redwood.NewClient("$REDWOOD_KEY", redwood.WithBaseURL("https://api.redwood.ai/v2"))
      out, _ := c.Generate(context.Background(), redwood.GenerateParams{Model: "redwood-embed-1", Prompt: "hello"})
      fmt.Println(out.Text)
    }

- D2 (endpoint migration + smoke tests):
  - Create v2 endpoints behind a feature flag. Start traffic shadowing: duplicate v1 traffic to v2 without impacting v1 responses.
  - Run A/B comparison on latency, token usage, and top-3 error buckets.
  - Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30–60 minute windows. Automate rollback if error rate > 1% or 95th pctl latency increases by >30%.

- D3 (retries/timeouts and rate limiting):
  - Recommended retry policy: up to 4 retries for idempotent requests, exponential backoff base=200ms, factor=2, max=5s with full jitter.
  - Pseudocode for client retry with jitter:
    function backoff(attempt) {
      const base = 200 // ms
      const max = 5000
      const jitter = Math.random() * base * Math.pow(2, attempt)
      return Math.min(max, jitter)
    }

  - Use idempotency-key header for non-idempotent calls: Idempotency-Key: <uuidv4>
  - Timeout defaults: connect=2s, read=10s for generation; tune down for short prompts.
  - Rate-limit handling: respect X-RateLimit-Remaining / X-RateLimit-Reset; when Remaining==0, pause until reset + small backoff.

- D4 (cutover rehearsal + production rollout):
  - Run production-like load for 15m in a rehearsal window (off-peak).
  - Confirm fallback works (flip canary to 0% and ensure requests route back to v1).
  - Schedule 2-hour cutover window with on-call for both teams.

Practical notes on batching & cost: enable small request batching (2–4 requests) for embeddings to reduce per-unit cost; for latency-sensitive flows keep batch size at 1 and tune model selection. We'll pre-suggest quantization profile if you want to run on Dedicated later.

If helpful, Monica and I can run a 60-minute workshop with your infra team tomorrow afternoon — ping preferred times and we'll book.

— Monica
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: AstraPay integration: SDK setup, endpoint migration & retry strategy

Thanks Monica — that plan looks solid. A couple of implementation notes from infra: 

- We'll open a sandbox CIDR (10.18.32.0/24) for your IPs; please provide final CIDR list so we can update the firewall rule.
- Rate-limit headers we publish: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (unix epoch seconds). If Remaining drops below 10, we will start returning 429.
- For our rollout constraints, we prefer progressive canary with 15-minute holds at each step. If you can adjust the rollback trigger to error rate > 0.8% and 95th pctl latency increase > 25%, we can be conservative.

One operational question: what is your recommended behavior if a burst causes sustained 429s? Should clients switch to a lower-capacity model variant automatically or pause requests? We prefer an explicit instruction to avoid unexpected behavior.

Thanks — we'll stand by for the final IPs and the sandbox keys. Proposed time for the 60-minute workshop: Wed 09:30–10:30 PT.

— AstraPay Platform Team
